content.text:
I fixed `parse_date` in `dates/parse.py`, and all 3 tests in `tests/test_parse.py` now pass.

The old format string didn't allow a trailing `Z`, which caused the `ValueError`. `parse_date` now strips a trailing `Z` and returns a UTC-aware datetime. Timestamps without a `Z` still parse to naive datetimes as before, so `test_naive` and `test_day_key` are unaffected.

Only `parse_date` and `day_key` use it, so nothing else needed changing. Comparing a `Z` timestamp with a naive one will raise a `TypeError`, which is standard Python behavior for mixed aware and naive datetimes.
